summary: An independent code-review audit of the Big Walk redesign (release-fragments/unreleased/big-walk-real-ui.json) found and this fixes: an infinite refetch loop hammering Pulse's insights/weekly aggregation queries every 20 seconds forever, an unconfirmed/possibly-inverted 'assist' badge, Players/Sessions nav cards that always landed on empty pages for a local-save game, and a games-list card that mislabeled an unsampled container server as local-save.
details: The server-detail page's graph, weekly/insights, and world effects depended on the `status` state object directly — fetchServerStatus allocates a new object every 20s poll tick, so those effects (added across the last two commits) re-ran and refetched on every tick instead of once per page view. Fixed by depending on stable derived primitives (status kind, last-uploaded timestamp) instead of the object identity; the world panel now also deliberately refetches when a new save upload actually lands, instead of never refreshing while the tab stays open.

The 'Assist off' badge asserted a meaning for `skipAidsActive` that nothing in Pulse documents and that reads as plausibly inverted from the raw field name — replaced with a literal 'Skip aids: on/off' readout that states the flag without interpreting it, matching this page's own no-invented-meaning standard for de-slugged labels.

Players and Sessions nav cards (built from container-log session tracking a local-save game has no config for) always led to well-formed empty pages for Big Walk — hidden for local-save games; Activity stays, since it's genuinely populated from the save-diff events.

The games list page inferred 'this is a local-save game' from `current === null`, which is also true for a container-backed game before its first metrics sample lands — now only renders the local-save card once a `/status` fetch actually confirms it, falling back to the ordinary container card (as an unsampled container server already did) until then.
